clue.text: I object being in the way, so went for a jaunt

indicators.note: one piece being in another means it sits inside it, here the object pronoun goes into the road

parts.note: a road is a way
the object form of the pronoun I is me

explanation.surface: Someone who objected to being in the way took themselves off on an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' looks like someone protesting; it is grammar, the pronoun I in its object form, and 'being in' sets that inside the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander about at leisure, which is what an outing for pleasure involves.

clue.text: Feature of Methuselah in the big time?

explanation.surface: A question about what marked out the Bible's oldest man in some grand era.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is the Bible's longest-lived man; 'the big time' is read as a great span of years, not success.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah is famous for living 969 years, an extreme old age; a big stretch of time is likewise a long age.

clue.text: Once Grandpa goes the event 0 is upset

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the three opening words are rearranged

explanation.surface: When Grandpa leaves, the family occasion is spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is upset' rearranges the letters of ONCE GRANDPA GOES, all fifteen of them.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic school sports-day race in which runners balance an egg on a spoon.

clue.text: The power of understanding the feelings of others, and making them pay for it

definitions.text: The power of understanding the feelings of others

indicators.note: making these words into something else means reworking their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Understanding how others feel, yet still charging them for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' signals that the letters of THEM PAY are rearranged; 'for it' just rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the standard dictionary sense: the ability to share and understand another person's emotions.

clue.text: Doesn't take a reproof sitting down, apparently

definitions.text: Doesn't take a reproof sitting down, apparently

parts.words: Doesn't take a reproof sitting down, apparently
parts.note: read literally, someone rebuked who rises to their feet; the idiom means accepting that one was in error

explanation.surface: Someone who refuses to accept criticism meekly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not taking it sitting down' usually means resisting; here the person is literally on their feet while being put right, which is the idiom for admitting a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit one was wrong after being put right is the idiom's meaning, and the person is standing up while doing so.

clue.text: Broken lances on the site where Harold fell

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, so the letters of the weapons are reassembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Shattered spears littering the battlefield where King Harold died in 1066.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges LANCES. The Battle of Hastings in 1066, where the English King Harold was killed, was fought on Senlac Hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Senlac Hill is the historic name for the ridge where the Battle of Hastings was fought and Harold was killed.

clue.text: Collective reports from all quarters .

parts.note: north is one of the four quarters of the compass
east is one of the four quarters of the compass
west is one of the four quarters of the compass
south is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Reports gathered from every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The four compass points, North, East, West and South, give one letter each. The clue runs on into 14 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports of recent events are, taken together, a collective noun for current information.

clue.text: Fly over the river at Leicester

explanation.surface: Flying above a river running through an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester is a city in the English Midlands, and the River Soar flows through it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly is to rise high in the air; the second sense is the name of the river that flows through Leicester.

clue.text: We hear James is at the keep-fit place

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Jim is a short form of the name James

explanation.surface: Gossip says James is at the fitness centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' signals a homophone: JIM, the short form of James, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnasium is a hall for exercise, and the short form is the usual word for a fitness centre.

clue.text: What we have here point to scholastic exercises

parts.note: things at hand are these
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Things right here point to academic work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What we have here' is a roundabout way of saying THESE; a compass point gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissertations are written arguments produced as academic exercises.

clue.text: Wild animal retreating around the motorway

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters of the combined pieces run in the opposite direction

parts.note: read as 'a round', which is a lap of a course
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A wild beast backing away around a busy road.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'around' as 'a round', A LAP; add MI (the M1, the main motorway north from London) and 'retreating' turns the whole run back.
explanation.definitionFit: An African antelope is a wild animal of the savanna.

clue.text: Girl with an inclination to be a chronicler

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an is the article a
a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A girl inclined to be a record-keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' is not a liking here but a tilt: a ship that lists leans over.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes yearly records of events is a writer of history.

clue.text: First as Prince of Wales, however

definitions.text: First as Prince of Wales, however

parts.words: First as Prince of Wales, however
parts.note: the king who was the first English heir given the title Prince of Wales, yet only the second king of his name

explanation.surface: A remark about who held the Welsh princely title first.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward I's son was made the first English Prince of Wales in 1301; the twist is that as king he was not first but second. 'however' marks that contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: The son of Edward I was the first heir to bear the title Prince of Wales and became the second King Edward.

clue.text: … most of which isn't used

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter, so the tail is dropped

parts.note: the ellipsis carries on from 7 down, and which refers to the reports of that clue

explanation.surface: Most of those reports haven't been put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 7 down: 'which' stands for that answer, and 'most of' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fresh and unworn has never been put to use.

clue.text: Met punk rocker 8 a dishevelled state

indicators.note: a rocker shakes things up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Meeting a punk rock musician looking scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocker' looks like a musician but signals rearranging MET PUNK.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy, uncombed hair and clothes describe someone scruffy and messy.

clue.text: A religious kind of pigeon

explanation.surface: A devout sort of dove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A religious' is a noun here: a member of a religious order. There is also a fancy breed of pigeon with this name, from its hooded markings.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in a convent is a religious in the noun sense; the pigeon breed is named for its hood, like a sister's veil.

clue.text: Information from the underworld?

explanation.surface: Intelligence from the criminal world.
explanation.walkthrough: The underworld is literally far beneath us, so it is low down; the slang word for inside facts is spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside facts are the true details on something; the underworld is deep below, at a low level.

clue.text: Handily placed trysting-tree?

parts.note: a tree whose name pairs a romantic appointment with the inside of the hand

explanation.surface: A conveniently located tree where lovers meet.
explanation.walkthrough: A tryst is a date, and 'handily' points to the palm of the hand; together they name the fruit tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree that bears dates has a name combining a lovers' appointment with the hand's inner surface.

clue.text: Mounted a step

parts.note: a stride is a long step

explanation.surface: Climbing up a step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' means sitting with legs either side, as on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with one leg on each side, as a rider sits a horse, is the mounted position.

clue.text: Inverted amounts in quiet style

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Inverted amounts in quiet style': the answer is an anagram of INVERTED AMOUNTS, but no other word signals the anagram, so 'Inverted' would be both fodder and indicator.

clue.text: Scope of a disused temporary shelter

parts.note: ex means former, no longer in use
a tent is a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: The size of an abandoned camping shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disused' gives EX, the prefix for former.
explanation.definitionFit: Range and reach are synonyms for how far something stretches.

clue.text: Finished after five, having made a sale

indicators.note: one piece after another means it follows it, so the numeral comes first

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
ended means finished

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper finished after five o'clock, with a sale made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places ENDED behind V, the Roman five.
explanation.definitionFit: To vend is to sell, so something vended has been sold.

clue.text: One who may reprimand at some length

definitions.text: One who may reprimand at some length

parts.words: One who may reprimand at some length
parts.note: a person who delivers a long telling-off; also a university teacher giving talks

explanation.surface: Someone given to long scoldings.
explanation.walkthrough: To lecture someone is to scold them at length; the word also means an academic teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives long talks, whether teaching or scolding, is the person in question.

clue.text: Tie up about ten and go off

indicators.note: one piece put about another goes round it, so the reversed word wraps the numeral
in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the word tie, taken as written
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Fasten something round ten and depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TIE to EIT, and 'about' wraps it round X, the Roman ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave the stage, as an actor does, is a departure.

clue.text: Managing to cover a course in masonry

explanation.surface: Succeeding in roofing a layer of brickwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the capping layer on top of a wall, which covers the top course of stone or brick.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting by is managing; the capping on a wall is the top row of stones that covers the masonry beneath.

clue.text: Computerised man has part of Nairobi on integrated circuit

indicators.note: part of the words means only a stretch of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: A robot man contains a piece of the Kenyan capital on a microchip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' takes BION from 'NairoBI ON', then IC is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Having electronic or mechanical body parts makes someone a cyborg-like, technologically enhanced person.

clue.text: Currency mark on the billiard-table

explanation.surface: A money symbol found on a games table.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British pennies were marked d; the semicircle drawn at one end of a billiard or snooker table is also called the D. The answer is the letter spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter d was the symbol for an old penny, and the semicircular marking at the baulk end of a billiard table is named for that letter.

clue.text: Vegetable in Staffordshire

explanation.surface: A garden crop grown in an English Midlands county.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffordshire is a county in the English Midlands; Leek is a market town in it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an onion-family vegetable, the emblem of Wales; it is also the name of a market town in that county.
